title: Roasted Apricot and Almond Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Roasted apricot purée stirred into a lighter custard; toasted flaked almonds folded in.
summary: A lighter version of our classic custard, with a purée of oven-roasted apricots stirred in before churning and toasted flaked almonds folded through. Tangy, jammy and nutty.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Roast the apricots
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Toss the apricots with 60 g sugar in the tin, arrange cut side up and roast for 20-25 min until soft and caramelised at the edges; roasting concentrates their flavour and drives off water. Cool, blend smooth and chill.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Warm the cream, milk and salt until steaming. Whisk the yolks with 90 g sugar, whisk in two ladles of the hot dairy and pour back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook gently, stirring all the time, until a line drawn on the coated spatula holds and the thermometer shows 77-80 °C. Do not let it bubble.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Sieve, add the vanilla and cool over the iced water, then refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Stir in the cold apricot purée and churn until thick, then fold in the toasted almonds by hand.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pack into the container and freeze for at least 4 h. The fruit flavour is brightest within a week.

tips: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3-4 min, shaking often, until golden.
A common mistake is adding warm purée to the base, which slows churning and gives an icy result. Chill both parts.
Very ripe, slightly soft apricots give the best colour and flavour.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 1 week. Soften for 10 min at room temperature before scooping.
